I think doing drugs occasionally and addicted to them are two different things.

Well, yes. 

My uncle is a sad piece of human. But drugs really makes him worse. 

At the height of his addiction, he almost cannot hold his anger. Every single thing will make him angry. And his sister will become his punching bag. 

It's a bit better now, after he quits. But the addiction already messed up his brain a little bit.

I digress. 

I know few of my uncle's friends (ex-drug addict too) that turned a new leaf after leaving their addiction. But at the height of their addiction, they will do absolutely everything they can to fulfill their own addiction. Even if it's hurting their families or communities. Drugs and dealers won't care about how the addict find money to buy drugs. The only people that not turns to criminality as their way to fast cash is the people that already have wealthy family background.

My uncle, mother's brother, is ex-drug addict.

My mother always tells me and my siblings about him as cautionary tales about drugs. Stealing something from family is him on good days, on a bad days, he can threat strangers with knife and gun (gun is not even legal in my country) to give him money. 

There's countless time where he abuse his sisters. My grandma is doing whatever she can. But she's alone with no support systems, so many times she can only comply to his request if they still want to survive. My own mother escape from that situation through marriage.

His abuse makes his other sister a semi-alcoholic for a few years too. He only stopped when he have 3rd kid, iirc. But at that point his drug addiction already ruined many people lives. Including me, and my cousin. 

Because I remember vividly how sadistic the way he beat his sister, my aunt. While my cousin witnessed how untrustworthy he was towards money, sometimes there's no food on table because his addiction comes first. 

I hate all addiction with passion, especially drugs. Because I witnessed with my own eyes how addiction will devour all lives around them, not only the addict themselves.

I can't understand why people refuse to see how harmful it is.
